A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SWD research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite extensive revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original spectral analyses, image-generation experiments, runtime measurements, ablations, and human preference studies in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original image and video generation experiments, expanded spectral and loss analyses, runtime measurements, and human preference studies.

M1.justification: v2 extends spatial SWD to joint spatial and temporal generation, adding frame-count schedules and adjacent-frame blending during latent upsampling (Section 4.1, Appendix C). This extends the training and sampling procedure beyond images. The underlying per-image patch-mean loss is retained despite PDM being renamed MMD; newly documented feature noising does not alone establish a change to the earlier implementation.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates image generation, whereas v2 additionally trains and evaluates text-to-video generation using Wan2.1-generated videos, MovieGenBench, and VBench-2.0. COCO2014, MJHQ, PartiPrompts, and GenEval image coverage remains. The earlier internal real-data training comparison is removed.

E2.justification: The image comparisons add Hyper-SD and SD3.5-M-Turbo, plus FLUX comparisons involving Schnell, Turbo-Alpha, and Hyper-FLUX (v2 Table 3). The new video comparison evaluates Wan2.1 and CausVid, with CausVid retrained on the authors' synthetic dataset (Table 2). These substantially expand the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Image evaluation replaces CLIP Score with HPSv3. Reported training changes from 5K iterations and batch size 80 to approximately 3K iterations and model-dependent batches of 64 or 24. The main SD3.5-Large configuration also changes its step and scale schedule. New protocols include video evaluation on 1003 MovieGenBench prompts and patch-based image-quality metrics.

E4.justification: v2 adds batch-averaging and noising ablations for MMD, human comparisons of MMD-only training, high-frequency detail tests, spatial-only versus spatiotemporal video scaling, and expanded spectral and upsampling-ratio analyses. Constant-scale tests are expanded. Conversely, v1's explicit time-shift, no-scale-wise-training, real-data, and naive token-wise loss ablations are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions average runtime measurements over 100 independent runs and collect three assessor responses per image pair with majority voting. Human preference plots contain error bars in both. No changed seed, confidence-interval, significance-testing, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial SDXL, FLUX, video, and supplementary-analysis results and revises existing image, runtime, and ablation entries. For example, Table 1's upscale-before-noising FID-5K at t=800 changes from 13.0 to 14.7. The new video Table 2 reports SWD at 1.8 seconds/video and VideoReward 6.27. Changed training and timing documentation prevents interpreting the revised tables as isolated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The kernel-based MMD expression in v2 restates the earlier mean-embedding definition, and the patch-mean loss remains mathematically equivalent. However, the explicit naive token-wise loss definition in v1 Appendix C, Equation 3, is removed with that comparison. Neither version supplies formal guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: Video generation moves from future work in v1 to a central demonstrated contribution in v2, including joint spatial-temporal scaling and an approximately threefold same-step video speedup claim. v2 also explicitly claims that the MMD objective improves convergence. The original claims of efficient progressive generation and a useful standalone patch loss remain.

C2.justification: v2 substantially qualifies the earlier low-resolution teacher discussion: DMD can inherit teacher failures, while MMD and GAN objectives enable recovery (Appendix B). It also explains conditional-information loss from batch averaging, acknowledges that spectral analysis cannot determine schedules by itself, and discusses the defect tradeoff of MMD-only training. These materially clarify mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Appendices A and C provide expanded model-specific feature layers, MMD noising intervals, adapter ranks, synthetic-data generation settings, and sampling schedules. Appendix G newly discloses TinyVAE use for runtime measurements. Conversely, v1's explicit 500K synthetic-sample count and fake-score guidance value are no longer specified. These are substantial documentation changes, including both gains and losses.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises positioning around progressive diffusion and MMD, adding discussions of f-DM, Relay Diffusion, pyramidal flow matching, DMMD, IMM, and GAN feature matching. It presents SWD as extending an existing progressive-diffusion research line, replacing v1's broader differentiation from previous diffusion approaches. The earlier standalone discussion of dynamic token-routing methods is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method narrative are extensively rewritten. PDM becomes MMD terminology; DMD2 implementation material moves to Appendix A, and the low-resolution teacher discussion moves from Section 5.1 to Appendix B. Experiments are reorganized to present main comparisons first, followed by full-resolution comparisons and focused MMD ablations.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to a single-column conference format. Benchmark tables are regrouped by model family, timing information is split into separate tables, and spectral, video, and loss-analysis displays are added. Existing training/sampling diagrams are relocated, while the four assessor-interface screenshots are enlarged onto separate appendix pages.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for generality and detail preservation through broader image/video validation and targeted loss, spectral, and upsampling analyses. Its explanation of low-resolution teacher failures and model-specific implementation guidance resolves important applicability gaps in v1. These gains outweigh the removed controls and dataset-size disclosure, although numerical consistency remains imperfect: spatial-only SWD's VBench score is 52.8 in Table 2 but 52.43 in Table 12.
